newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM says Isasmelt copper smelter shut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM says Isasmelt copper smelter shut.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it has shut down its Isasmelt copper smelter for immediate repair work.
Production will continue with the second primary smelter, the company said.
Copper anode output for the year ending June 30 will meet the company's forecast of 177,000 tonnes, it said.
The net effect of the shutdown, required to replace furnace bricks, will be about a 30 percent reduction in output for an estimated 25 days, an MIM spokeswoman told Reuters.
"The shutdown will not impact on the copper smelter's budgeted output, which will remain at 177,000 tonnes of anode" MIM said.

"Given the record production of 95,000 tonnes in the first half of the financial year, we were forcasting in excess of budget if the rebrick were to have taken place in the next financial year," MIM said.
The furnace bricks are progressively consumed as part of the normal operation of the smelting process, MIM said.
MIM said the shutdown was moved forward from a scheduled date of between May and July after a section of brick collapsed in the furnace.
The next major shutdown involving parts of the smelter is planned for November 1997, the company said.

MIM is in the process of lifting overall smelting capacity to about 250,000 tonnes a year to accommodate additional intermediate concentrate supplies from expanded operations at Mount Isa and from the nearby Ernest Henry copper mine.
